articles.title: Spike in oil prices partly reverses rupee rally, forward premiums surge
articles.content: The Indian rupee has faced depreciation as a result of escalating oil prices combined with pressures from surrounding currencies. With Brent crude exceeding $96 per barrel, worries about India's import costs and inflation have intensified. Recent days have seen heightened hedging activity among importers, leading analysts to forecast potential testing of the rupee's support levels. Additionally, banks are urging central bank intervention to manage the growing dollar surplus.

articles.title: Rupee falls 20 paise to 92.40 against US dollar in early trade
articles.content: The rupee fell 20 paise to 92.40 against the US dollar in early trade. Higher crude oil prices and proposed tariffs by the US administration increased dollar demand. Foreign fund inflows supported the rupee but it faced pressure from rising crude prices. The US proposed 25 percent tariffs on imports from India, which raised inflation concerns. India rejected these allegations and expressed commitment to finalize a bilateral trade deal.

articles.title: India bonds tumble as Brent tops $95 per barrel, RBI flags food inflation risks
articles.content: Indian government bonds fell as oil prices surged, raising concerns about inflation and economic stability. The Reserve Bank of India highlighted rising food inflation pressures, indicating widespread price increases. Higher oil prices may widen the current account deficit and impact the rupee negatively. Investors are anticipating the monetary policy decision scheduled for December 4, with rate hikes expected. The overall economic situation reveals significant inflation challenges ahead for the country.

articles.title: South Korea's central bank resumes tightening with quarter-point hike
articles.content: The Bank of Korea raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point to 3.25%. This increase follows a pause in October and is part of the tightening cycle. articles.title: LME steps in to ease squeeze in aluminium market
articles.content: On Tuesday, the London Metal Exchange changed its trading rules to address the aluminium market squeeze. This situation has caused consumers to pay the highest prices for immediate supplies in decades. The market squeeze is largely due to a decline in LME inventories, mostly controlled by a few participants. One entity holds a significant percentage of all LME aluminium warrants, influencing market dynamics.

articles.title: Deutsche Bank, PNB ink pact to fund M&As
articles.content: Deutsche Bank and Punjab National Bank have signed a preliminary agreement to finance corporate acquisitions in India. This partnership follows recent reforms that allow domestic lenders to fund up to 75% of corporate deal values. State Bank of India has also entered a similar partnership with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group. The agreement aims to support Indian companies in their growth and strategic expansion efforts.
